record.notes: The Minister of Electronics and IT announced the institute at a media interaction at Electronics Niketan, New Delhi, on 30 January 2025, adopting what he called a techno-legal approach, together with the empanelment of over 18,000 GPUs and a call for proposals for indigenous foundation models; the IndiaAI article on it is dated 31 January 2025. The institute is incubated by the IndiaAI Mission under its Safe and Trusted pillar. The India AI Governance Guidelines of November 2025 (IN-02) describe the recently established institute as the main body for guiding the safe and trusted development and use of AI in India: it should do research, risk assessment and capacity-building, test and evaluate AI systems for risks, advise policymakers and industry, and anchor India's participation in the International Network of AI Safety Institutes.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026. The official_url (IndiaAI article on indiaai.gov.in) could not be stored on any attempt (robots.txt unreachable, DNS failures, then a TLS certificate that could not be verified). Stored instead: the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser's PDF copy of that article (psa.gov.in, the secondary_url, dated 31 Jan 2025); the PIB release of MeitY of 30 Jan 2025 (PRID 2097709, pib.gov.in) with its annexures, and a PSA copy of the same release; and the India AI Governance Guidelines (static.pib.gov.in). The PIB release confirms the announcement by the minister on 30 Jan 2025, the Safe and Trusted pillar, the mandate, the hub-and-spoke model and the second Expression of Interest themes (watermarking and labelling, AI risk assessment and management, stress-testing tools, deepfake detection) used in the summary. The guidelines confirm the institute's later role. No stored source gives the institute's legal form or a date of formal operational launch.
